ns2:section.sectionText: This course examines the conceptual issues associated with citizenship and immigration, considering current political debates from a variety of perspectives, empirical, historical, and normative. The majority of the course will focus on the United States, but we will also examine the immigration and citizenship practices of other nations as well. Among the topics to be considered include why people migrate; consequences of migration; efforts to integrate immigrants? socially, culturally, and politically? into their host societies; public opinion about immigration and immigrants; various citizenship traditions and rationales; membership, belonging, and national identity; and postnational citizenship. Not intended for students with Freshman class standing. Students may not receive more than three hours of credit for PS 300. This special topics course lies within the Comparative Politics subfield.
